meta.corpus: 37 California DOI bulletins (data/processed/ca), 129 chunks in insurance_ca_v1
meta.description: Phase 2 retrieval eval set. Each in-scope question maps to the doc_id(s) whose text actually contains the answer. Out-of-scope questions have an empty relevant_doc_ids list and are scored only on top-1 retrieval score (Phase 3 guardrail-threshold tuning). Grown from 28 to 61 questions on 2026-09-16 (pre-Phase-6 hardening: 19 new bulletins ingested, 33 new questions added covering them and new near-duplicate clusters).

categories.temporal_disambiguation: correct bulletin among near-duplicates that differ by year/date
categories.out_of_scope: plausible insurance question, not covered by any bulletin in the corpus

questions.question: What is the Fiscal Year 2024-25 Life principle-based reserving annual aggregate assessment amount?
Which California Insurance Code section authorizes the Long-Term Care principle-based reserving annual aggregate assessment?
questions.note: CIC section 1067.11(4)(j)

questions.question: During a declared state of emergency, what is the minimum number of days an insurer must give an insured to submit proof of loss?
questions.note: 100 days from date of loss; CIC 2051.5(b)(3)(A)

questions.question: Which Senate Bill amended Insurance Code section 2051.5 to extend the proof of loss deadline during a state of emergency?
questions.note: SB 495 (Ch. 542, Stats. of 2025)

questions.question: Under Assembly Bill 144, within how many business days must a health insurer begin covering a newly recommended CDPH immunization?
questions.note: 15 business days after CDPH publishes the recommendation

questions.question: What coverage category was added to the California Export List in 2025?
questions.note: Commercial Cannabis Related Operations; Foster Family entry also modified

questions.question: What is the adjusted minimum net worth amount for the commercial insured exemption effective January 1, 2025?
What did the California Supreme Court decision in Another Planet establish about coverage for smoke damage claims?
questions.note: smoke damage can be covered where policy insures 'direct physical loss of or damage to' property

questions.question: What does Senate Bill 805, the No Vigilantes Act, prohibit bail fugitive recovery agents from doing?
questions.note: using their position for immigration enforcement, or disclosing PII for immigration enforcement, absent a judicial warrant/court order

questions.question: Which wildfire led to the mandatory moratorium covering Mono County in December 2025?
questions.note: Pack Fire; declaration December 9, 2025; ZIPs 93512, 93514, 93529, 93546

questions.question: What five-year CPI-U percentage change was used for the 2025 commercial insured exemption adjustment?
According to Bulletin 2025-11, which rate arrangements likely violate the prior approval provisions of Proposition 103?
questions.note: negotiated or mutually-agreed-upon rates, retrospective rating plans, Large Risk Alternative Rating Options (LRAROs), consent-to-rate

questions.question: Which bulletin extends the wildfire cancellation and non-renewal moratorium to commercial property insurance, and which statute authorizes that extension?
questions.note: SB 547 (Perez); Insurance Code section 675.55; effective January 1, 2026

questions.question: What is the FY 2024-25 Long-Term Care PBR annual aggregate assessment amount?
What is the difference between the Life and the Long-Term Care principle-based reserving annual aggregate assessments for FY 2024-25?
questions.note: Life $3,188,000 vs LTC $1,433,000; different CIC sections and premium basis; different tier tables

questions.question: How did the Life principle-based reserving annual aggregate assessment change from FY 2024-25 to FY 2025-26?
How did the Long-Term Care principle-based reserving annual aggregate assessment change from FY 2024-25 to FY 2025-26?
Bulletin 2025-11 and Bulletin 2026-2 both concern Proposition 103 rate compliance - what distinct violation does each address?
questions.note: 2025-11: negotiated rates / retro plans / LRAROs / consent-to-rate without filed & approved factors. 2026-2: unauthorized modification of Department proprietary formulas in rate templates/exhibits

questions.question: Which Insurance Code sections authorize the Life assessment versus the Long-Term Care assessment under principle-based reserving?
What is the Life principle-based reserving annual aggregate assessment for fiscal year 2025-26?
Which moratorium bulletin concerns the Franklin Fire, and on what date was that state of emergency declared?
questions.note: declared June 18, 2025 (Malibu); must not return the other 5 near-identical moratorium bulletins

questions.question: In the Long-Term Care principle-based reserving bulletin issued in May 2025, what was the aggregate assessment amount?
questions.note: $1,433,000 (FY 2024-25) - must not return 2026-4 (issued May 2026)

questions.question: Which 2026 bulletin addresses the wildfire moratorium for the Gifford Fire?
questions.note: Gifford Fire; SLO & Santa Barbara counties; declared December 23, 2025

questions.question: What are New York's requirements for personal auto insurance rate filings?
questions.note: wrong state; corpus is CA only

questions.question: How does a beneficiary file a life insurance death benefit claim in California?
questions.note: consumer claims process; not a bulletin topic in this corpus

questions.question: What is the minimum paid-in capital required to license a new property and casualty insurer in California?
questions.note: solvency/licensing requirement; not in corpus

questions.question: Does California law require earthquake coverage to be offered to homeowners insurance policyholders?
questions.note: real CA law (CIC 10081) but not covered by any bulletin in this corpus - topically plausible distractor

questions.question: What are the continuing education requirements for a licensed California insurance producer?
questions.note: licensing/CE requirement; not in corpus

questions.question: Which fires triggered the residential property insurance cancellation/non-renewal moratorium announced in Bulletin 2025-1, and on what date did the Governor's emergency declaration take effect?
questions.note: Palisades, Eaton, Hurst, Lidia, Sunset, Woodley, and Olivas Fires; Governor's emergency declaration January 7, 2025 covering Los Angeles and Ventura counties; moratorium ZIP codes listed for each fire

questions.question: Under California Insurance Code section 10103.7(b), what is the minimum percentage and dollar cap for the advance payment insurers must offer for contents coverage after a total loss, without requiring an itemized claim?
questions.note: no less than 30 percent of the policy limit applicable to the covered dwelling structure, up to a maximum of $250,000 (Cal. Ins. Code section 10103.7[b])

questions.question: What is the 'efficient proximate cause' doctrine, and which California Insurance Code section codifies it according to Bulletin 2025-3?
questions.note: Insurance Code section 530: an insurer is liable for a loss of which a peril insured against was the proximate cause, even though an uncovered peril may have been a remote cause; applied to wildfire-caused mudslide/landslide/flood claims, citing Julian v. Hartford Underwriters Ins. Co. and Howell v. State Farm Fire & Casualty Co.

questions.question: What was the total dollar amount of the FAIR Plan assessment approved via Commissioner Order 2025-1, and what percentage of that assessment may member insurers recoup from policyholders under Bulletin 2025-4?
questions.note: $1 billion assessment approved by Order 2025-1, the first FAIR Plan assessment on member insurers in over 30 years; member insurers may recoup 50% of the assessment paid, provided it was not covered by reinsurance or reimbursed through other means

questions.question: Under California Insurance Code section 12401, how many days after receipt by the Commissioner must a title insurance rate filing's effective date be delayed, at minimum?
questions.note: the effective date shall not be earlier than the 30th day following its receipt by the commissioner (CIC section 12401); the rate must also be publicly displayed for no less than 30 days per section 12401.7

questions.question: What was the Long-Term Care principle-based reserving annual aggregate assessment for Fiscal Year 2023-24?
questions.note: $1,406,000; issued as Bulletin 2024-2, dated May 10, 2024, under CIC section 1067.11(4)(j)

questions.question: Did the California Department of Insurance make any changes to the Export List in the 2023 annual renewal process described in Bulletin 2024-1?
questions.note: No - after the 2023 public hearing and comment period, the Commissioner decided not to make any changes to the Export List

questions.question: What was the Life principle-based reserving annual aggregate assessment for Fiscal Year 2023-24?
questions.note: $2,666,000, established under CIC section 10489.992(b)(4), dated May 10, 2024

questions.question: Under California Insurance Code section 706.7, what is a 'reciprocal state,' and how often must the Commissioner notify domestic insurers of the list of reciprocal states?
questions.note: a state whose laws prohibit an insurer domiciled there from insuring the lives/persons of CA residents or property located in CA unless the insurer holds a valid CA certificate of authority; the Commissioner must mail notice to every domestic insurer every four years specifying reciprocal states (28 states/territories listed, e.g. Alaska, Colorado, Florida)

questions.question: Which fire and county triggered the moratorium in Bulletin 2024-5, and on what date did it begin?
questions.note: Thompson fire, Butte County; Governor's emergency declaration July 3, 2024; moratorium begins July 3, 2024

questions.question: Which three wildfires and counties are covered by the moratorium described in Bulletin 2024-6?
questions.note: Gold Complex Fire (Plumas County) and Park Fire (Butte and Tehama Counties), both declared July 26, 2024; Borel Fire (Kern County), declared July 30, 2024

questions.question: Under the rate application review procedure announced in Bulletin 2024-7, how long does the Department have to initially review a complete rate application after it is placed on Public Notice, and how many 30-day extensions are allowed?
questions.note: the Department shall review the file within 60 days of the filing's Public Notice date, with up to two additional 30-day extensions after the original 60-day period

questions.question: Under the FAIR Plan recoupment procedure established in Bulletin 2024-8, what percentage of an assessment up to $1 billion may a member insurer recoup, and what percentage applies above that threshold?
questions.note: up to 50% recoupment for assessments up to $1 billion for residential or commercial lines (or up to $2 billion combined); 100% recoupment of any portion of the assessment exceeding those thresholds

questions.question: Which wildfires does the 2nd Amended Bulletin 2024-9 cover, and on what dates were the underlying states of emergency declared?
questions.note: Line Fire (San Bernardino County, declared September 7, 2024); Bridge Fire (LA/San Bernardino Counties) and Airport Fire (Orange/Riverside Counties), both declared September 11, 2024; bulletin supplements the original September 19, 2024 bulletin

questions.question: Did the California Department of Insurance make any changes to the Export List in the 2024 annual renewal process described in Bulletin 2024-10?
questions.note: No - after the 2024 public hearing and comment period, the Commissioner decided not to make any changes to the Export List

questions.question: Which fire and county are addressed by the moratorium in Bulletin 2024-11, and what ZIP codes are covered?
questions.note: Boyles Fire, Lake County, declared September 29, 2024; ZIP codes 95422, 95423, 95451, 95457, 95679, 95987

questions.question: Which two fires and counties does Bulletin 2024-12 address, and when were the emergency declarations made?
questions.note: Shelly Fire (Siskiyou County) and Bear Fire (Sierra County), both declared November 1, 2024

questions.question: Which fire and county does Bulletin 2024-13 address, and when did the moratorium begin?
questions.note: Mountain Fire, Ventura County; Governor's emergency declaration November 7, 2024; moratorium begins November 7, 2024

questions.question: According to Bulletin 2024-14, what must an insurer do regarding credit card convenience fees before charging them to policyholders?
questions.note: disclose all such fees as part of a complete rate application and obtain the Department's prior approval before charging such fees; this bulletin expressly supersedes Bulletin No. 79-6

questions.question: How did the FAIR Plan assessment recoupment procedure in Bulletin 2025-4 relate to the general procedure established in Bulletin 2024-8?
questions.note: 2024-8 established the general recoupment procedure and percentage tiers (50% recoupment up to $1B/$2B combined thresholds, 100% above) before any assessment had occurred since 1994; 2025-4 applied and updated that procedure after Commissioner's Order 2025-1 actually approved a $1 billion FAIR Plan assessment following the January 2025 Palisades/Eaton fires, allowing 50% recoupment and requiring the 'FPA-2025' program designation and a six-month filing deadline

questions.question: How did the Life principle-based reserving annual aggregate assessment change from FY 2023-24 to FY 2024-25?
How did the Long-Term Care principle-based reserving annual aggregate assessment change from FY 2023-24 to FY 2024-25?
Across the 2023, 2024, and 2025 Export List bulletins, in which year did the Department first add or modify a coverage category, and what was the change?
questions.note: the 2023 renewal (Bulletin 2024-1) and 2024 renewal (Bulletin 2024-10) made no changes to the Export List; the 2025 renewal (Bulletin 2025-16) added 'Commercial Cannabis Related Operations' and modified 'Foster Family (Occurrence Based Only)' to 'Foster Family and Foster Family Agency Liability'

questions.question: Bulletins 2025-2 and 2025-3 both address wildfire-related claims from the January 2025 Southern California fires - what distinct legal issue does each cover?
questions.note: 2025-2 addresses advance claim payment obligations after a total loss (ALE advance payment, contents-without-inventory advance payment, full benefits for rebuilding at a new location, extended time limits to collect replacement cost/ALE); 2025-3 addresses the 'efficient proximate cause' doctrine (Ins. Code section 530) for flood/mudslide/earth movement claims where wildfire was the covered triggering peril

questions.question: Which moratorium bulletin concerns the Thompson fire, and in which county?
questions.note: Thompson fire, Butte County, declared July 3, 2024 - must not return the other near-identical moratorium bulletins in the corpus (2024-6, 2024-9, 2024-11, 2024-12, 2024-13, 2025-1, 2025-12, 2025-17, 2026-1)

questions.question: Which bulletin addresses the moratorium arising from the Gold Complex, Park, and Borel Fires together?
questions.note: Bulletin 2024-6, covering Plumas County (Gold Complex Fire) and Butte/Tehama Counties (Park Fire), both declared July 26, 2024, and Kern County (Borel Fire), declared July 30, 2024

questions.question: Which 2nd Amended moratorium bulletin covers the Line, Bridge, and Airport Fires?
questions.note: Bulletin 2024-9 (rev), 2nd Amended, dated October 15, 2024, supplementing the original September 19, 2024 bulletin - must not return other fire-name moratorium bulletins

questions.question: Which moratorium bulletin covers the Boyles Fire in Lake County?
questions.note: Bulletin 2024-11, declared September 29, 2024, Lake County, ZIP codes 95422, 95423, 95451, 95457, 95679, 95987

questions.question: Which moratorium bulletin covers both the Shelly Fire and the Bear Fire?
questions.note: Bulletin 2024-12, November 1, 2024 declarations - Shelly Fire in Siskiyou County and Bear Fire in Sierra County

questions.question: Which moratorium bulletin addresses the Mountain Fire in Ventura County?
questions.note: Bulletin 2024-13, declared November 7, 2024, Ventura County - must not return the Franklin Fire bulletin (2025-12), also in a nearby area but a different fire and date

questions.question: Which amended moratorium bulletin covers the Palisades, Eaton, Hurst, Lidia, Sunset, Woodley, and Olivas Fires from January 2025, and how many times was it amended?
questions.note: Bulletin 2025-1, marked 'Amended*'; originally issued January 9, 2025, amended January 14, 2025, and again January 17, 2025 to add ZIP codes - must not return the other fire-name moratorium bulletins
